items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: So he dragged me along one day and he made me play for Fats. I was about 16 or 17, in the basement of the theater.

ctx.x: Um what I mean was that Baltimore normally would not be a good place to grow up in music, it wasn’t any main scene. There were two scenes, there was a white jazz scene and a black jazz scene, which is not unusual, that’s the American Way at that time, and I gravitated, there was a very lively black scene down the strip called Pennsylvania Avenue which was sort of the 125th Street of Baltimore. And they had a theater which was the Baltimore counterpart of the Apollo. It was called the Royal Theater. And everybody…
You got it in your ear.
